impl.deviations:
1. The merge commit (1427e9007f) carries three pieces of PR 4959 behaviour inside Ben's operations that the brief placed in commits 2 and 3: (a) the short-run policy inside page::set_k_block (16 valid lanes -> store_block with the full mask and the block recorded as converted; fewer lanes -> set_k_row per lane, which follows the block's recorded layout), (b) the dense gate inside page::try_score_k_amx (declines unless every block of the page is converted), (c) the tail-block split inside page::score_k (converted blocks to k_vnni::qk_group, row-major blocks to the dotter, through one score_rows lambda and the private k_vnni_token_mask). Reason: with PR3''s set_k_block and PR 4959's layout state, the merged code would have written VNNI columns for every run while get_k_row, score_k's callers and the forward-end conversion take the layout from the block bit (block_to_vnni would then transpose bytes that were already VNNI), and the dispatch test's 'full page with unrecorded rows: no kernel call' expectation would fail at the merge commit. Each conflict hunk was resolved the way PR2' resolved its kernel-call hunk: the PR 4959 side's semantics placed inside the cache operation. Commits 2 and 3 therefore carry the remaining reshaping only (commit 2: eagle_storage_slots naming, store_block's caller comment; commit 3: k_plan_copy / copy_k_rows / for_each_vnni_k_block helpers, k_vnni_blocks for every geometry).
2. note_k_block_saved was inlined into set_k_block and deleted in the merge (the operation records the block itself; no caller remained). The block is recorded on every KV head's set_k_block call (idempotent fetch_or; the first call sets the bits) instead of after the last KV head as PR 4959 did: the page does not know which head is last. The Note states why no reader can observe the state between the heads' calls (the block's 16 tokens are the pass's own and are marked complete only after the store).

impl.summary: Against PR 4959's head (6b081187e1) the branch merges PR3' (2c501a9390) and re-expresses the tail-block work on Ben's structure in 8 commits, each green on the 22-cell matrix. self_attention.hpp and full.hpp are the PR3' side (Ben's token loop with one page::score_k call, the bool gate of apply_dense_amx_page, k_head_fn always copying through get_k_row); no layout word remains in them. The page owns every layout decision: set_k_block stores 16 rows with store_block and records the block as converted, and stores shorter runs row by row in the block's recorded layout; try_score_k_amx declines a page with a row-major block; score_k gives converted blocks to k_vnni::qk_group and row-major blocks to the dotter. note_k_row_saved answers a page-owned token (std::optional<k_pending_block>) that k_block_to_vnni takes; k_storage_ref and k_storage_of are private; model.hpp records rows inside its mark loop with no layout clause, and resize() reserves the pending list with a derived bound. copy_storage_slot plans its bits once per slot (k_plan_copy) and moves rows through copy_k_rows; k_forget_row and the conversion share for_each_vnni_k_block; eagle_storage_slots follows the file's naming. The per-row operations of a row-major block live in tron::detail; k_vnni_view states that at(), store_row and load_row are defined for converted blocks only. Tests use one helper (test::record_k_row_and_convert), no raw plane access, no #ifdef around k_vnni_blocks (which exists for every geometry), and enum classes instead of three bools; the row-major build now asserts that no block is ever VNNI. README.ci.md documents TRON_AMX_DISABLE (the kill switch keeps the layout) and the rebuild a rollback needs; the Note bullets and the reader comment name page::score_k as the tail scorer. Stored bytes, scores and test expectations are unchanged; the deb preset flip and benchmark rows are already in the base.

pr_body_facts: self_attention.hpp keeps Ben's token loop: it fills one 64-bit live mask, calls page::score_k once, and apply_dense_amx_page returns the answer of page::try_score_k_amx, so no layout name (k_vnni::, k_packed, k_vnni_blocks, block_bit, offset_bit, row_major_row, __mmask16) remains on a code line of self_attention.hpp, model.hpp or full.hpp.

page::try_score_k_amx declines (returns false, scores and storage untouched) a VNNI slot whose four 16-token blocks are not all converted, read from the private k_vnni_blocks_ state, and the caller then scores the page in software at the cost of the 1 KiB zero-fill of s_pages (tensor<4, 64>'s constructor) that apply_dense_amx_page performs before the call.

page::score_k splits the live mask by the page's converted-block bits (private k_vnni_token_mask): the tokens of converted blocks go to k_vnni::qk_group, and the tokens of row-major blocks and of row-major slots go to the dotter through one score_rows lambda that builds the dotter array only when it has rows.

page::set_k_block is the one K store that store_k_block (model.hpp) calls, once per run of next_k_run and KV head, with a std::array of row views where an invalid view marks an absent lane: 16 valid rows take store_block (a register transpose and 64 whole-line stores) and the page records the block's 16 row bits and block bit itself, fewer rows take set_k_row per row (into the row-major block, or into the VNNI column of a converted block), and a row-major slot stores per lane in place.
